```{r Create output directory structure}
# ============================================================================
# MASTER OUTPUT DIRECTORY STRUCTURE
# ============================================================================

output_dir  <- "DEG_results"

# Sub-folders
qc_dir                  <- file.path(output_dir, "QC")
contrasts_dir           <- file.path(output_dir, "Contrasts")
clusters_dir            <- file.path(output_dir, "Clusters")
loops_dir               <- file.path(output_dir, "Loops")
comp_dir                <- file.path(output_dir, "Compartments")
comp_enrichr_dir        <- file.path(comp_dir, "enrichr_compartments")

# Motif sub-folders (created here; homer paths defined later)
homer_promoter_dir      <- file.path(clusters_dir, "homer_promoter_motifs")
homer_chip_dir          <- file.path(clusters_dir, "homer_chip_motifs")

# Gene-list sub-folders
contrasts_genelists_dir <- file.path(contrasts_dir, "enrichment_gene_lists")
clusters_genelists_dir  <- file.path(clusters_dir,  "enrichment_gene_lists")

for (d in c(qc_dir, contrasts_dir, clusters_dir, loops_dir, comp_dir,
            comp_enrichr_dir, homer_promoter_dir, homer_chip_dir,
            contrasts_genelists_dir, clusters_genelists_dir)) {
  if (!dir.exists(d)) dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE)
}
```

```{r Pre-DESeq2 PCA - All samples including dec25 GFP}

# ── Paths ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
star_dec25 <- "R:/R_STIK/rna_seq/rnaseq_marta_REHAro_dec25/STAR"
star_mar26 <- "R:/R_STIK/rna_seq/rnaseq_marta_REHArg_mar26/STAR"

# ── Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
read_star_counts <- function(file) {
  df     <- read.table(file, skip = 4, header = FALSE)
  counts <- df[, 2]
  names(counts) <- gsub("\\..*", "", df$V1)
  return(counts)
}

load_star_dir <- function(dir_path, exclude_pattern = NULL) {
  files <- list.files(dir_path, pattern = "ReadsPerGene.out.tab$", full.names = TRUE)
  if (!is.null(exclude_pattern))
    files <- files[!grepl(exclude_pattern, basename(files))]
  sample_names <- gsub("^STAR_(.*)ReadsPerGene\\.out\\.tab$", "\\1", basename(files))
  counts_list  <- lapply(files, read_star_counts)
  names(counts_list) <- sample_names
  return(counts_list)
}

# ── Load all samples from both runs ─────────────────────────────────────────
counts_dec25_full <- load_star_dir(star_dec25)   # includes dec25 GFP
counts_mar26_full <- load_star_dir(star_mar26)   # includes mar26 GFP

# Disambiguate GFP names before merging
gfp_pattern <- "^RNA-REH-GFP-"
names(counts_dec25_full) <- ifelse(
  grepl(gfp_pattern, names(counts_dec25_full)),
  paste0(names(counts_dec25_full), "_dec25"),
  names(counts_dec25_full)
)
names(counts_mar26_full) <- ifelse(
  grepl(gfp_pattern, names(counts_mar26_full)),
  paste0(names(counts_mar26_full), "_mar26"),
  names(counts_mar26_full)
)

all_counts_full   <- c(counts_dec25_full, counts_mar26_full)
counts_mat_full   <- do.call(cbind, all_counts_full)
sample_names_full <- colnames(counts_mat_full)

cat("Samples loaded from dec25:", length(counts_dec25_full), "\n")
cat("Samples loaded from mar26:", length(counts_mar26_full), "\n")
cat("Total samples in matrix  :", ncol(counts_mat_full), "\n")
cat("Sample names:\n"); cat(paste0("  ", sample_names_full, "\n"))

# ── Gene symbol annotation + deduplication ──────────────────────────────────
symbols_full <- mapIds(
  org.Hs.eg.db,
  keys      = rownames(counts_mat_full),
  column    = "SYMBOL",
  keytype   = "ENSEMBL",
  multiVals = "first"
)

valid_syms            <- !is.na(symbols_full)
counts_full_sym       <- counts_mat_full[valid_syms, ]
rownames(counts_full_sym) <- symbols_full[valid_syms]

counts_full_sym           <- as.data.frame(counts_full_sym)
counts_full_sym$symbol    <- rownames(counts_full_sym)
rownames(counts_full_sym) <- NULL
counts_full_sym$mean_expr <- rowMeans(counts_full_sym[, sample_names_full])

counts_full_sym <- counts_full_sym %>%
  group_by(symbol) %>%
  slice_max(mean_expr, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

counts_full_sym$mean_expr <- NULL
counts_full_sym            <- as.data.frame(counts_full_sym)
rownames(counts_full_sym)  <- counts_full_sym$symbol
counts_full_sym$symbol     <- NULL

coldata_full <- data.frame(
  row.names = colnames(counts_full_sym),

  condition = c(
    rep("REH",  3),
    rep("Aro",  3),
    rep("EP1",  3),
    rep("GFP",  3),
    rep("Arg",  3),
    rep("d189", 3),
    rep("d89",  3),
    rep("GFP",  3)
  ),

  batch = c(
    rep("batch1", 3),
    "batch1", "batch1", "batch2",
    "batch1", "batch1", "batch2",
    rep("batch1", 3),
    rep("batch3", 3),
    rep("batch3", 3),
    rep("batch3", 3),
    rep("batch3", 3)
  ),

  highlight = c(
    rep("REH",       3),
    rep("other",     6),   # fixed
    rep("GFP_dec25", 3),
    rep("other",     9),
    rep("GFP_mar26", 3)
  )
)

stopifnot(identical(rownames(coldata_full), colnames(counts_full_sym)))

# ── VST (blind, intercept-only — purely exploratory) ────────────────────────
dds_explore <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = counts_full_sym,
  colData   = coldata_full,
  design    = ~ 1
)
dds_explore <- dds_explore[rowSums(counts(dds_explore)) > 5, ]
vsd_explore  <- vst(dds_explore, blind = TRUE)

# ── PCA ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pca_data   <- plotPCA(vsd_explore, intgroup = c("condition", "batch"), returnData = TRUE)
percentVar <- round(100 * attr(pca_data, "percentVar"))

# Attach highlight column for Plot 2
pca_data$highlight <- coldata_full[rownames(pca_data), "highlight"]

# Plot 1 — all 24 samples, condition + batch
p_all <- ggplot(pca_data, aes(PC1, PC2, color = condition, shape = batch, label = name)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_text_repel(size = 3, max.overlaps = 40) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(batch1 = 16, batch2 = 17, batch3 = 15)) +
  theme_bw() +
  xlab(paste0("PC1 (", percentVar[1], "% variance)")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2 (", percentVar[2], "% variance)")) +
  ggtitle("PCA – All 24 samples (VST blind)\nColour = condition | Shape = batch")
print(p_all)
ggsave(file.path(qc_dir, "PCA_all24_condition_batch.pdf"), p_all, width = 10, height = 7)

# Plot 2 — GFP (dec25 vs mar26) and REH highlighted
p_highlight <- ggplot(pca_data, aes(PC1, PC2, label = name)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = condition, shape = batch), size = 4, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(
    data = pca_data[pca_data$highlight != "other", ],
    aes(fill = highlight),
    shape = 21, size = 5, color = "black", stroke = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(size = 3, max.overlaps = 40) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(batch1 = 16, batch2 = 17, batch3 = 15)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(GFP_dec25 = "#FFD700", GFP_mar26 = "#1f78b4", REH = "#33a02c"),
    name   = "Highlighted group",
    labels = c(GFP_dec25 = "GFP batch1/dec25",
               GFP_mar26 = "GFP batch3/mar26",
               REH       = "REH batch1 (control)")
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  xlab(paste0("PC1 (", percentVar[1], "% variance)")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2 (", percentVar[2], "% variance)")) +
  ggtitle("PCA – GFP and REH highlighted\ngold = GFP dec25 | blue = GFP mar26 | green = REH")
print(p_highlight)
ggsave(file.path(qc_dir, "PCA_all24_GFP_REH_highlight.pdf"), p_highlight, width = 10, height = 7)

cat("Pre-DESeq2 PCA saved to", qc_dir, "\n")
```

```{r REH vs GFP_mar26 - correlation check, independent of PCA outlier effects}
# ============================================================================
# Direct similarity check: is REH ~ GFP (mar26) once the dec25 GFP outlier
# is excluded from the picture?
# Uses vsd_noGFPdec25 (21 samples) — same VST object behind the
# PCA_21samples_no_dec25GFP plot, so this is consistent with that figure
# and is NOT affected by the PC1 distortion caused by the dec25 GFP outlier
# seen in the 24-sample PCA.
# ============================================================================

vsd_mat <- assay(vsd_noGFPdec25)

# Restrict to the genes used for PCA (ntop = 500, matches plotPCA default)
# so the correlation reflects the same "most variable genes" signal driving
# the PCA plot, rather than being diluted by thousands of near-flat genes
rv       <- apply(vsd_mat, 1, var)
ntop     <- 500
top_genes <- names(sort(rv, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(ntop, length(rv)))]

cor_mat <- cor(vsd_mat[top_genes, ], method = "pearson")

# ── Pairwise sample correlation heatmap ─────────────────────────────────────
ann_col <- coldata_noGFPdec25[colnames(cor_mat), c("condition", "batch")]

p_corr_heatmap <- pheatmap(
  cor_mat,
  annotation_col   = ann_col,
  annotation_row   = ann_col,
  main             = "Sample-sample correlation (top 500 variable genes)\n21 samples, dec25 GFP removed",
  fontsize_row     = 7,
  fontsize_col     = 7
)
ggsave(file.path(qc_dir, "Correlation_heatmap_21samples.pdf"),
       p_corr_heatmap, width = 9, height = 8)

# ── Summarise: average correlation of REH vs each other condition ──────────
reh_samples <- rownames(coldata_noGFPdec25)[coldata_noGFPdec25$condition == "REH"]

reh_vs_condition <- sapply(levels(factor(coldata_noGFPdec25$condition)), function(cond) {
  cond_samples <- rownames(coldata_noGFPdec25)[coldata_noGFPdec25$condition == cond]
  # exclude REH-vs-REH self pairs when summarising REH's own block
  if (cond == "REH") {
    vals <- cor_mat[reh_samples, reh_samples]
    vals <- vals[lower.tri(vals)]
  } else {
    vals <- as.vector(cor_mat[reh_samples, cond_samples])
  }
  mean(vals)
})

reh_vs_condition_df <- data.frame(
  condition          = names(reh_vs_condition),
  mean_corr_with_REH = round(reh_vs_condition, 4)
) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_corr_with_REH))

cat("Mean correlation of REH samples vs each condition (top 500 var genes):\n")
print(reh_vs_condition_df)

cat("\nIf GFP (mar26) sits at the top (closest to REH, excluding REH itself),\n",
    "that supports REH ≈ GFP as equivalent controls.\n",
    "If GFP is no closer to REH than Arg/d189/d89/Aro/EP1, the apparent\n",
    "similarity seen in the 24-sample PCA was likely an artifact of the\n",
    "dec25 GFP outlier compressing PC1 scaling, not genuine biological equivalence.\n", sep = "")
```

```{r STAR counts}
# ============================================================================
# STAR COUNTS - merged from two sequencing runs
# dec25 folder : all samples EXCEPT STAR_RNA-REH-GFP*
# mar26 folder : STAR_RNA-REH-GFP*  +  every other sample in that folder
# ============================================================================

# star_dec25 <- "/ijc/LABS/STIK/RAW/rna_seq/rnaseq_marta_REHAro_dec25/STAR"
# star_mar26 <- "/ijc/LABS/STIK/RAW/rna_seq/rnaseq_marta_REHArg_mar26/STAR"

star_dec25 <- "R:/R_STIK/rna_seq/rnaseq_marta_REHAro_dec25/STAR"
star_mar26 <- "R:/R_STIK/rna_seq/rnaseq_marta_REHArg_mar26/STAR"

# --- helper: read a single STAR ReadsPerGene file --------------------------
read_star_counts <- function(file) {
  df     <- read.table(file, skip = 4, header = FALSE)
  counts <- df[, 2]
  names(counts) <- gsub("\\..*", "", df$V1)   # strip Ensembl version suffix
  return(counts)
}

# --- load samples -----------------------------------------------------------
# dec25: exclude GFP samples (they come from mar26 instead)
counts_dec25 <- load_star_dir(star_dec25, exclude_pattern = "STAR_RNA-REH-GFP-")

# mar26: all samples present (includes the GFP samples)
counts_mar26 <- load_star_dir(star_mar26)

# --- merge into one matrix --------------------------------------------------
# Combine both lists; mar26 entries will overwrite if names clash (they won't
# here because dec25 already has GFP excluded, but this is safe practice)
all_counts <- c(counts_dec25, counts_mar26)
# all_counts <- counts_mar26

counts_mat  <- do.call(cbind, all_counts)
sample_names <- colnames(counts_mat)

# cat("Samples loaded from dec25 :", length(counts_dec25), "\n")
cat("Samples loaded from mar26 :", length(counts_mar26), "\n")
cat("Total samples in matrix   :", ncol(counts_mat),     "\n")
cat("Sample names:\n"); cat(paste0("  ", sample_names, "\n"))
```

```{r gene symbol annotation}
# Map Ensembl IDs to gene symbols
ensembl_ids <- rownames(counts_mat)
symbols <- mapIds(
  org.Hs.eg.db,
  keys    = ensembl_ids,
  column  = "SYMBOL",
  keytype = "ENSEMBL",
  multiVals = "first"
)

# Keep only genes with valid gene symbols (remove NAs)
valid_symbols <- !is.na(symbols)
cat(paste("Total genes:", length(symbols), "\n"))
cat(paste("Genes with valid symbols:", sum(valid_symbols), "\n"))
cat(paste("Genes removed (no symbol):", sum(!valid_symbols), "\n\n"))

# Filter counts matrix to keep only genes with valid symbols
counts_sym <- counts_mat[valid_symbols, ]
rownames(counts_sym) <- symbols[valid_symbols]

# Convert to dataframe for deduplication
counts_sym        <- as.data.frame(counts_sym)
counts_sym$symbol <- rownames(counts_sym)
rownames(counts_sym) <- NULL

# Calculate mean expression across the 21 samples and deduplicate
# (keeping the row with highest mean expression per gene symbol)
counts_sym$mean_expr <- rowMeans(counts_sym[, sample_names])   # explicit column selection
counts_sym <- counts_sym %>%
  group_by(symbol) %>%
  slice_max(mean_expr, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()
cat(paste("Final unique genes after deduplication:", nrow(counts_sym), "\n"))

# Clean up and restore rownames
counts_sym$mean_expr <- NULL
counts_sym           <- as.data.frame(counts_sym)
rownames(counts_sym) <- counts_sym$symbol
counts_sym$symbol    <- NULL

# Confirm column order is preserved
stopifnot(identical(colnames(counts_sym), sample_names))
```

```{r DESeq2 Object - REH and GFP pooled as Control, batch-corrected}
# ============================================================================
# Per PI: REH and GFP (mar26) are treated as biological equivalents
# (empty-vector / parental controls) and pooled into a single "Control"
# condition. Because Control now spans batch1 (REH) AND batch3 (GFP_mar26),
# batch is no longer perfectly confounded with condition for this group,
# which means ~ batch + condition can potentially be fit without the
# rank-deficiency problem we had before.
#
# IMPORTANT CAVEAT (kept here as a permanent reminder):
# Aro and EP1 still have ZERO representation in batch3. Any batch correction
# applied to Arg/d189/d89/GFP-derived contrasts vs Aro/EP1 is therefore an
# EXTRAPOLATION of the batch effect learned from Control, not something
# directly verified for those conditions. Treat Aro/EP1 vs {Arg,d189,d89}
# contrasts with caution even after this correction.
# ============================================================================

# ── Build merged coldata ─────────────────────────────────────────────────--
coldata_merged <- coldata_noGFPdec25
rownames(coldata_merged) <- gsub(
  "_mar26$",
  "",
  rownames(coldata_merged)
)
coldata_merged$condition <- as.character(coldata_merged$condition)
coldata_merged$condition[coldata_merged$condition == "GFP"] <- "Control"
coldata_merged$condition[coldata_merged$condition == "REH"] <- "Control"
coldata_merged$condition <- factor(coldata_merged$condition)

cat("New condition levels:\n")
print(table(coldata_merged$condition, coldata_merged$batch))

# ── Check design matrix rank BEFORE building dds ────────────────────────────
# This tells us up front whether ~ batch + condition is even fittable,
# rather than discovering a rank-deficiency warning/error later.
test_mm <- model.matrix(~ batch + condition, data = coldata_merged)
mm_rank <- qr(test_mm)$rank
mm_cols <- ncol(test_mm)

cat("\nDesign matrix: ", mm_cols, " columns, rank = ", mm_rank, "\n", sep = "")
if (mm_rank < mm_cols) {
  cat("WARNING: design matrix is RANK-DEFICIENT (", mm_cols - mm_rank,
      " redundant column(s)). ~ batch + condition will NOT fit as specified.\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("Design matrix is full rank — ~ batch + condition can be fit.\n")
}

# ── Build DESeq2 object with batch correction ───────────────────────────────
stopifnot(identical(rownames(coldata_merged), colnames(counts_sym)))

dds_batch <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = counts_sym,
  colData   = coldata_merged,
  design    = ~ batch + condition
)
dds_batch <- dds_batch[rowSums(counts(dds_batch)) > 5, ]
dds_batch$condition <- relevel(dds_batch$condition, ref = "Control")

# Run DESeq2
dds_batch <- DESeq(dds_batch)

cat("\nModel coefficients (resultsNames):\n")
print(resultsNames(dds_batch))

cat("\ndds_batch summary:\n")
print(dds_batch)
```
```{r PCA after batch correction (removeBatchEffect for visualization only)}
# ============================================================================
# Batch-corrected PCA — VISUALIZATION ONLY.
# DESeq2's actual DE testing already accounts for batch properly via the
# ~ batch + condition GLM in dds_batch; this chunk does NOT feed into any
# statistical test. It uses limma::removeBatchEffect() purely so we can see,
# on a PCA plot, how samples relate to each other once the estimated batch
# effect is subtracted out of the expression matrix.
# ============================================================================

# VST on dds_batch with blind = FALSE: uses the actual ~ batch + condition
# design to estimate dispersions (more appropriate now that we have a
# defensible design, vs the blind/intercept-only VST used for raw QC plots)
vsd_batch <- vst(dds_batch, blind = FALSE)

# Remove the batch term from the expression matrix for plotting purposes
mat_corrected <- assay(vsd_batch)
mat_corrected <- removeBatchEffect(
  mat_corrected,
  batch = vsd_batch$batch
)
assay(vsd_batch) <- mat_corrected

# ── PCA on batch-corrected matrix ───────────────────────────────────────────
pca_batch_corrected <- plotPCA(
  vsd_batch,
  intgroup   = c("condition", "batch"),
  returnData = TRUE
)
percentVar_bc <- round(100 * attr(pca_batch_corrected, "percentVar"))

p_batch_corrected <- ggplot(
  pca_batch_corrected,
  aes(PC1, PC2, color = condition, shape = batch, label = name)
) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_text_repel(size = 3, max.overlaps = 40) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(batch1 = 16, batch2 = 17, batch3 = 15)) +
  theme_bw() +
  xlab(paste0("PC1 (", percentVar_bc[1], "% variance)")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2 (", percentVar_bc[2], "% variance)")) +
  ggtitle("PCA – 21 samples, AFTER batch correction (removeBatchEffect)\nColour = condition | Shape = batch | Control = REH + GFP_mar26 pooled")
print(p_batch_corrected)
ggsave(file.path(qc_dir, "PCA_21samples_batchCorrected.pdf"),
       p_batch_corrected, width = 10, height = 7)

cat("Batch-corrected PCA saved to", qc_dir, "\n")
cat("\nNOTE: this plot is for visualization/QC)
```
```{r Correlation heatmap after batch correction}
# ============================================================================
# Sample-sample correlation heatmap on the BATCH-CORRECTED matrix
# (same removeBatchEffect-adjusted assay used for the post-correction PCA).
# This lets us directly check things the PCA can only hint at — e.g. whether
# Aro-batch1 and Aro-batch2 samples (or EP1-batch1/batch2) now correlate
# more tightly with each other than they did pre-correction, given batch2
# has only 1 replicate per condition and a weak correction estimate.
#
# As before: for VISUALIZATION/QC only, not used in any statistical test.
# ============================================================================

mat_corrected_top <- assay(vsd_batch)  # already batch-corrected, from prior chunk

# Restrict to top 500 variable genes, consistent with the PCA and the
# earlier pre-correction correlation heatmap, so the two are comparable
rv_bc     <- apply(mat_corrected_top, 1, var)
ntop      <- 500
top_genes_bc <- names(sort(rv_bc, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(ntop, length(rv_bc)))]

cor_mat_bc <- cor(mat_corrected_top[top_genes_bc, ], method = "pearson")

ann_col_bc <- as.data.frame(colData(vsd_batch)[, c("condition", "batch")])

p_corr_heatmap_bc <- pheatmap(
  cor_mat_bc,
  annotation_col = ann_col_bc,
  annotation_row = ann_col_bc,
  main           = "Sample-sample correlation AFTER batch correction\n(top 500 variable genes, 21 samples)",
  fontsize_row   = 7,
  fontsize_col   = 7
)
ggsave(file.path(qc_dir, "Correlation_heatmap_21samples_batchCorrected.pdf"),
       p_corr_heatmap_bc, width = 9, height = 8)

# ── Quick numeric check: within-condition correlation, batch1 vs batch2 ────
# For Aro and EP1, compare the 2 batch1 replicates against the 1 batch2
# replicate, before vs after correction, to see if the correction actually
# pulled them closer together
check_within_condition <- function(cond, cor_mat, label) {
  samples   <- rownames(ann_col_bc)[ann_col_bc$condition == cond]
  batch_lab <- ann_col_bc[samples, "batch"]
  b1 <- samples[batch_lab == "batch1"]
  b2 <- samples[batch_lab == "batch2"]
  if (length(b2) == 0) return(NULL)
  mean_corr <- mean(as.vector(cor_mat[b1, b2]))
  data.frame(condition = cond, stage = label, mean_corr_batch1_vs_batch2 = round(mean_corr, 4))
}

# Need the PRE-correction correlation matrix for comparison —
# recomputed here from vsd_noGFPdec25 with merged condition labels
pre_mat   <- assay(vsd_noGFPdec25)
rv_pre    <- apply(pre_mat, 1, var)
top_pre   <- names(sort(rv_pre, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(ntop, length(rv_pre)))]
cor_mat_pre <- cor(pre_mat[top_pre, ], method = "pearson")

before_after <- rbind(
  check_within_condition("Aro", cor_mat_pre, "Before correction"),
  check_within_condition("Aro", cor_mat_bc,  "After correction"),
  check_within_condition("EP1", cor_mat_pre, "Before correction"),
  check_within_condition("EP1", cor_mat_bc,  "After correction")
)

cat("Within-condition batch1 vs batch2 correlation, before vs after batch correction:\n")
print(before_after)
cat("\nHigher correlation after correction = batch2 samples pulled closer to their\n",
    "batch1 same-condition counterparts. Small or no change is expected given\n",
    "batch2 has only 1 replicate per condition, limiting how well its offset\n",
    "can be estimated.\n", sep = "")
```    
  
```{r Helper functions}

sig_label <- function(p) {
  case_when(
    is.na(p) | p >= 0.05 ~ NA_character_,
    p < 0.001 ~ paste0("p=", formatC(p, format = "e", digits = 1)),
    TRUE ~ paste0("p=", round(p, 3))
  )
}

#Process all contrasts
process_results <- function(res_unshrunk, res_shrunk, contrast_name) {
  
  # Convert unshrunk results to dataframe
  df <- as.data.frame(res_unshrunk)
  df$gene <- rownames(df)
  
  # Add shrunken LFC and SE
  df$lfc_shrunk  <- res_shrunk$log2FoldChange
  df$lfcSE_shrunk <- res_shrunk$lfcSE
  
  # Classify genes using:
  # - UNSHRUNKEN LFC for biological threshold
  # - UNSHRUNKEN padj for statistics
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      diffexpressed = case_when(
        log2FoldChange > 1 & padj < 0.05 ~ "UP",
        log2FoldChange < -1 & padj < 0.05 ~ "DOWN",
        TRUE ~ "NO"
      ),
      contrast = contrast_name
    )
  
  return(df)
}


# MODIFIED Volcano plot function - marks PBX1 and TCF3 regardless of significance
create_volcano <- function(df, contrast_name, n_label = 20) {
  # Prepare labels for top genes
  df$padj[df$padj == 0] <- 1e-300
  df <- df[!is.na(df$padj) & !is.na(df$log2FoldChange), ]
  
  # Get top significant genes (these are actual top DEGs)
  top_genes <- head(df[order(df$padj), "gene"], n_label)
  
  # Check if PBX1 and TCF3 exist in dataset and add them SEPARATELY for labeling
  special_genes <- c("PBX1", "TCF3")
  special_genes <- special_genes[special_genes %in% df$gene]
  
  # Combine top genes with special genes for labeling
  genes_to_label <- unique(c(top_genes, special_genes))
  
  df$delabel <- ifelse(df$gene %in% genes_to_label, df$gene, NA)
  
  # Create a special category for PBX1 and TCF3 for highlighting
  df$special_gene <- ifelse(df$gene %in% special_genes, df$gene, NA)
  
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = lfc_shrunk, y = -log10(padj), 
                      col = diffexpressed, label = delabel)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5) +
    # Highlight PBX1 and TCF3 with larger purple diamond points
    geom_point(data = df[!is.na(df$special_gene), ],
               aes(x = lfc_shrunk, y = -log10(padj)),
               color = "purple", size = 4, shape = 18) +
    geom_text_repel(
      data = df[!is.na(df$delabel), ],
      aes(fontface = ifelse(!is.na(special_gene), "bold", "plain")),
      color = "black",
      max.overlaps = 50,
      force = 1,
      box.padding = 0.5,
      point.padding = 0.5,
      size = 3,
      seed = 42
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("DOWN" = "blue", "NO" = "grey", "UP" = "red"),
      labels = c("Down-regulated", "Not significant", "Up-regulated")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Differential Expression:", contrast_name, "(LFC Shrinkage Applied)"),
      x = "Shrunken Log2 Fold Change",
      y = "-Log10 Adjusted P-value",
      caption = "LFC shrinkage: 'ashr' method"
    ) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), col = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), col = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.title = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14),
      plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1, face = "italic", size = 9)
    )
  
  return(p)
}

#Raw MA plots (QC control)
create_ma_plot_raw <- function(df, contrast_name) {
  
  df_filtered <- df[!is.na(df$padj) & !is.na(df$baseMean), ]
  
  p <- ggplot(df_filtered, aes(x = log10(baseMean + 1),
                               y = log2FoldChange,
                               col = diffexpressed)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("DOWN"="blue","NO"="grey","UP"="red")) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1,1), linetype="dashed") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
    labs(
      title = paste("MA Plot (RAW LFC):", contrast_name),
      x = "Log10 Mean Expression",
      y = "Raw Log2 Fold Change",
      caption = "Classical MA plot (no shrinkage)"
    ) +
    theme_classic()
  
  return(p)
}

#Shrunken MA plots for publications
create_ma_plot_shrunk <- function(df, contrast_name) {
  
  df_filtered <- df[!is.na(df$padj) & !is.na(df$baseMean), ]
  
  p <- ggplot(df_filtered, aes(x = log10(baseMean + 1),
                               y = lfc_shrunk,
                               col = diffexpressed)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("DOWN"="blue","NO"="grey","UP"="red")) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1,1), linetype="dashed") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
    labs(
      title = paste("MA Plot (Shrunken LFC):", contrast_name),
      x = "Log10 Mean Expression",
      y = "Shrunken Log2 Fold Change",
      caption = "LFC shrinkage: ashr"
    ) +
    theme_classic()
  
  return(p)
}
```

```{r Analysis - All Contrasts with LFC Shrinkage}
contrasts_list <- list(
  # vs EP1

)

all_results <- list()
cat("\n=== PERFORMING DESEQ2 WITH LFC SHRINKAGE ===\n")
for (contrast_name in names(contrasts_list)) {
  cat("Processing:", contrast_name, "\n")

  res_unshrunk <- results(dds_batch, contrast = contrasts_list[[contrast_name]])
  res_shrunk   <- lfcShrink(dds_batch, contrast = contrasts_list[[contrast_name]], type = "ashr")

  df <- process_results(res_unshrunk, res_shrunk, contrast_name)
  all_results[[contrast_name]] <- df

  # Summary
  cat("  Total DEGs:", sum(df$diffexpressed != "NO"), "\n")
  cat("  Upregulated:", sum(df$diffexpressed == "UP"), "\n")
  cat("  Downregulated:", sum(df$diffexpressed == "DOWN"), "\n")

  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

  # Manual MA plot - Unshrunken
  plot(log10(res_unshrunk$baseMean),
       res_unshrunk$log2FoldChange,
       pch = 16,
       cex = 0.4,
       col = ifelse(res_unshrunk$padj < 0.05 & !is.na(res_unshrunk$padj), "red", "gray60"),
       main = paste(contrast_name, "- Unshrunken"),
       xlab = "Log10 mean expression",
       ylab = "Log2 fold change",
       ylim = c(-5, 5))
  abline(h = 0, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

  # Manual MA plot - Shrunken
  plot(log10(res_shrunk$baseMean),
       res_shrunk$log2FoldChange,
       pch = 16,
       cex = 0.4,
       col = ifelse(res_shrunk$padj < 0.05 & !is.na(res_shrunk$padj), "red", "gray60"),
       main = paste(contrast_name, "- Shrunken (ashr)"),
       xlab = "Log10 mean expression",
       ylab = "Log2 fold change",
       ylim = c(-5, 5))
  abline(h = 0, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
}

summary_deg <- data.frame(
  Contrast   = names(all_results),
  Total_UP   = sapply(all_results, function(x) sum(x$diffexpressed == "UP")),
  Total_DOWN = sapply(all_results, function(x) sum(x$diffexpressed == "DOWN")),
  Total_DEG  = sapply(all_results, function(x) sum(x$diffexpressed != "NO"))
)
cat("\n=== SUMMARY OF DEGs ACROSS ALL CONTRASTS ===\n")
print(summary_deg)
```

```{r Enrichment Analysis with enrichR, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}

library(enrichR)

websiteLive <- getOption("enrichR.live", TRUE)
if (websiteLive) {
  dbs_available <- listEnrichrDbs()
}

dbs <- c("GO_Biological_Process_2023",
         "KEGG_2021_Human",
         "WikiPathway_2023_Human",
         "Reactome_2022",
         "MSigDB_Hallmark_2020")

# ============================================================================
# HELPER: robust gene-list extractor
# enrichR returns genes in the Genes column separated by ";" or "; " (with space)
# depending on the database and package version. This handles both reliably.
# ============================================================================
extract_genes <- function(genes_string) {
  # Split on semicolon (with or without surrounding spaces)
  genes <- unlist(strsplit(genes_string, "\\s*;\\s*"))
  # Remove any empty strings that could arise from trailing separators
  genes <- genes[nchar(trimws(genes)) > 0]
  trimws(genes)
}

# ============================================================================
# HELPER: clean enrichR result table
# Applies term-ID stripping (GO, Reactome, WikiPathway) uniformly and
# computes gene_ratio. Works for any database.
# ============================================================================
process_enrichr_db <- function(db_result) {
  df <- db_result %>%
    separate(col = "Overlap", into = c("Gene_count", "total"), sep = "/",
             convert = TRUE, extra = "drop", fill = "right")
  df$gene_ratio <- df$Gene_count / df$total
  # Strip embedded IDs from term names (present in GO, Reactome, WikiPathway)
  df$Term <- gsub("\\s*\\(GO:\\d+\\)", "",   df$Term)
  df$Term <- gsub("\\s*R-HSA-[0-9.]+",  "",  df$Term)
  df$Term <- gsub("\\s*WP\\d+",         "",  df$Term)
  df$Term <- trimws(df$Term)
  df
}

# ============================================================================
# HELPER: save gene lists + summary TSV for one direction x database x contrast
# ============================================================================
save_enrichr_genelists <- function(sig_terms, prefix, out_dir) {
  # One summary TSV with all significant terms
  sig_out <- sig_terms %>%
    select(Term, Gene_count, total, gene_ratio, P.value, Adjusted.P.value, Genes) %>%
    arrange(Adjusted.P.value)
  write.table(sig_out,
              file.path(out_dir, paste0(prefix, "_enrichment.tsv")),
              sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
}

# ============================================================================
# HELPER: bubble plot for enrichR results
# ============================================================================
plot_enrichr <- function(sig_terms, title_str, xlab_str) {
  plot_data <- head(sig_terms, 20)
  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Term, y = -log10(Adjusted.P.value))) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "azure4", size = 0.5) +
    geom_point(aes(size = Gene_count, colour = gene_ratio), alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = rev(plot_data$Term)) +
    scale_color_gradient(low = "green", high = "red", limits = c(0, NA)) +
    coord_flip() +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.ticks.length    = unit(-0.1, "cm"),
          axis.text.x          = element_text(margin = margin(5, 5, 0, 5, "pt")),
          axis.text.y          = element_text(margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5, "pt")),
          axis.text            = element_text(color = "black"),
          panel.grid.minor     = element_blank(),
          legend.title.align   = 0.5,
          plot.title           = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "black",
                                              face = "bold", size = 14)) +
    xlab(xlab_str) +
    ylab("-log10(Adjusted P-value)") +
    labs(color = "Gene Ratio", size = "Number\nof genes") +
    ggtitle(title_str)
}

# ============================================================================
# MAIN LOOP
# ============================================================================
all_enrichr_results <- list()

for (contrast_name in names(all_results)) {
  
  cat("\n=== Processing enrichR for:", contrast_name, "===\n")
  
  df       <- all_results[[contrast_name]]
  dge_up   <- subset(df, diffexpressed == "UP")
  dge_down <- subset(df, diffexpressed == "DOWN")
  cat("UP genes:", nrow(dge_up), "| DOWN genes:", nrow(dge_down), "\n")
  
  for (direction in c("UP", "DOWN")) {
    
    dge_set <- if (direction == "UP") dge_up else dge_down
    if (nrow(dge_set) == 0 || !websiteLive) next
    
    enriched <- enrichr(as.vector(dge_set$gene), dbs)
    all_enrichr_results[[paste0(contrast_name, "_", direction)]] <- enriched
    
    for (db_idx in seq_along(dbs)) {
      db_name <- dbs[db_idx]
      
      if (is.null(enriched[[db_idx]]) || nrow(enriched[[db_idx]]) == 0) next
      
      # Process: clean terms + compute gene_ratio
      enriched_processed <- process_enrichr_db(enriched[[db_idx]])
      sig_terms <- subset(enriched_processed, Adjusted.P.value < 0.05)
      
      if (nrow(sig_terms) == 0) {
        cat("  No significant results for", db_name, direction, "\n")
        next
      }
      
      # File prefix: <contrast>_<direction>_<db>
      file_prefix <- paste0(contrast_name, "_", direction, "_", db_name)
      
      # Save gene lists + summary TSV
      save_enrichr_genelists(sig_terms, file_prefix, contrasts_genelists_dir)
      
      # Plot + save
      p <- plot_enrichr(
        sig_terms,
        title_str = paste(db_name, "-", contrast_name, paste0("(", direction, ")")),
        xlab_str  = paste(db_name, "Terms", paste0("(", direction, ")"))
      )
      print(p)
      ggsave(
        file.path(contrasts_dir,
                  paste0("enrichR_", db_name, "_", direction, "_", contrast_name, ".pdf")),
        p, width = 10, height = 7
      )
      cat("  Plot + gene lists saved for", db_name, direction, "\n")
    }
  }
}

cat("\n=== enrichR analysis completed for all contrasts ===\n")
```
